title: The plant kingdom and plant groups
summary: Plant groups from mosses to flowering plants, alternation of generations, and monocots and dicots
cards.0.h: What makes a plant a plant
cards.0.p: Plants are eukaryotic and multicellular. Their cell walls are made of cellulose. They make food by photosynthesis and store the extra as starch. They protect their embryos inside a tissue.
cards.0.key: Chlorophyll a and b and cellulose are also found in green algae. Protecting the embryo, however, is unique to land plants. That is why they are called embryophytes.
cards.0.once.soru: In what form does a plant store the extra food it makes by photosynthesis?
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.neden: Glucose molecules join to form starch. Potatoes and wheat are examples of this store.
cards.0.once.secenekler.1.neden: Glycogen is the storage substance of animals and fungi.
cards.0.once.secenekler.2.neden: Cellulose is not a storage substance. It is the building material of the cell wall.
cards.1.p: Plants living on land faced the problems of drying out, moving water and reproducing. The cuticle reduced water loss, stomata controlled gas exchange and vascular bundles carried water. Pollen and seeds freed reproduction from depending on water.
cards.1.key: Vascular bundles are made of xylem and phloem. These features appeared step by step: mosses have no vascular bundles, and ferns have no seeds.
cards.2.p: Plants are grouped by two questions: does it have vascular bundles, and does it have seeds? These questions separate nonvascular plants, seedless vascular plants and seed plants.
cards.2.key: Mosses and liverworts are nonvascular. Ferns, horsetails and club mosses are seedless vascular plants. No group is nonvascular and also has seeds.
cards.2.etk.soru: Put each plant in the right group.
cards.2.etk.ogeler.2.2: A fern has vascular bundles, but no seeds. It reproduces with spores.
cards.2.etk.ogeler.5.2: A pine is a gymnosperm. Its seed sits exposed on a cone scale.
cards.3.p: Mosses and liverworts have no vascular bundles and no true roots, stems or leaves. They hold on with rhizoids and stay short. Their sperm reach the egg by swimming through water, so they live in damp places.
cards.3.key: Rhizoids mainly serve to anchor the plant. A moss absorbs water through its whole surface. Mosses, together with lichens, are among the pioneer species that first settle on bare rock.
cards.3.once.soru: Why do mosses mostly live in damp, shady places?
cards.3.once.secenekler.0.neden: For fertilization, the sperm must swim through water to the egg. Also, a moss has no vascular bundles to carry water.
cards.3.once.secenekler.1.neden: Mosses carry out photosynthesis, so they need light.
cards.3.once.secenekler.2.neden: Mosses have no true roots. They hold on with rhizoids.
cards.4.p: Ferns, horsetails and club mosses have xylem and phloem. They form true roots, stems and leaves. However, these plants have no seeds or flowers. They reproduce with spores.
cards.4.svg#2: on the underside of the leaf
cards.4.key: Their sperm swim in water, so most of them live in damp places.
cards.4.once.soru: What are the brown dots on the underside of a fern leaf?
cards.4.once.secenekler.0.neden: A fern does not make seeds. Spores form inside these sacs.
cards.4.once.secenekler.2.neden: These are the plant's normal reproductive structures.
cards.5.h: Alternation of generations: gametophyte and sporophyte
cards.5.p: A 2n cell has two of each chromosome, and an n cell has one. In alternation of generations, the 2n sporophyte makes spores by meiosis. A spore grows into the n gametophyte, and the gametophyte makes gametes.
cards.5.svg#17: fern: sporophyte is the large plant, gametophyte is the prothallus
cards.5.key: Mitosis keeps the chromosome number the same, while meiosis halves it. In plants, spores form by meiosis. Gametes form by mitosis in the gametophyte, and the 2n zygote grows into a sporophyte again.
cards.6.h: How did the dominant generation change?
cards.6.p: As you just saw, the gametophyte is dominant in mosses and the sporophyte is dominant in ferns. In seed plants, the gametophyte stays microscopic. Pollen is the male gametophyte, and the embryo sac is the female gametophyte.
cards.6.key: A fern's gametophyte is a small but independent plant called the prothallus. A pollen grain is not a sperm. It is a tiny male gametophyte that makes sperm.
cards.7.p: In seed plants, pollen is carried by wind or animals, so fertilization does not depend on water. A seed is made of an embryo, stored food and a coat. It can wait through drought and sprouts when conditions are right.
cards.7.svg#6: pollen is carried: fertilization does not need outside water
cards.7.key: A spore is a single cell. A seed is a multicellular structure made of an embryo, stored food and a coat.
cards.7.once.soru: What advantage does a seed have over a spore?
cards.7.once.secenekler.0.neden: A seed holds an embryo, a store of food to nourish it and a protective coat. A spore is a single cell.
cards.7.once.secenekler.1.neden: A spore is a single cell, so it is much lighter than a seed.
cards.7.once.secenekler.2.neden: A spore forms by meiosis, while a seed develops after fertilization.
cards.8.p: Pine, spruce, fir and juniper are gymnosperms. Their seeds sit exposed on cone scales. These plants have no flowers or fruits, and their pollen is carried by the wind. Most stay green all year.
cards.8.svg#0: seeds on the inner face of the scale
cards.8.key: The grape-like "berry" of a juniper is not a true fruit. It is a cone whose fleshy scales have fused.
cards.9.p: In angiosperms, the ovule is protected inside the ovary, and the ovary becomes the fruit. Double fertilization happens only in this group. One sperm forms the zygote, and the other forms the endosperm, the food tissue in the seed.
cards.9.key: In double fertilization, a sperm joins the egg to form the 2n zygote. The other sperm joins the two polar nuclei to form the 3n endosperm.
cards.9.once.soru: Which part of the flower does a cherry fruit develop from?
cards.9.once.secenekler.0.neden: After fertilization, the ovary becomes the fruit, and the ovule inside it becomes the seed.
cards.9.once.secenekler.1.neden: The petals fall off after fertilization.
cards.9.once.secenekler.2.neden: Pollen is the male gametophyte, and it does not become a fruit.
cards.10.h: Monocots and dicots: stems and leaves
cards.10.p: Angiosperms are divided by their number of cotyledons, or seed leaves. In monocots, leaf veins are parallel and vascular bundles are scattered. In dicots, veins form a network, bundles are arranged in a ring and there is a cambium.
cards.10.key: The cambium makes the stem thicker and forms the annual rings. A palm is a monocot. It has no cambium and no annual rings.
cards.10.once.soru: A plant has leaves with parallel veins. Which group is it in?
cards.10.once.secenekler.0.neden: Parallel veins are a sign of monocots. Wheat, corn and tulips are examples.
cards.10.once.secenekler.1.neden: In dicots, the veins form a network.
cards.10.once.secenekler.2.neden: The cotyledon split is used only for angiosperms.
cards.11.h: Monocots and dicots: roots and flowers
cards.11.p: Monocots have fibrous roots, and their flower parts come in multiples of 3. Wheat and tulips are examples. Dicots have a taproot, and their flower parts come in multiples of 4 or 5. Beans and roses are examples. To identify a plant, look at several features together.
cards.11.key: A tulip has 6 tepals and is a monocot. A wild rose has 5 petals. Corn and palms are monocots, while oaks and sunflowers are dicots.
cards.12.p: Plants are the producers on land. They release oxygen and take up CO2. Their roots prevent erosion. They give people food, timber, fiber and medicine. Coal also formed from ancient plant forests.
cards.12.svg#14: photosynthesis is the base of food chains on land
cards.12.key: Peat moss (Sphagnum) builds up in bogs and forms peat.
cards.12.once.soru: When the trees on a slope are cut down, which problem gets worse?
cards.12.once.secenekler.0.neden: Roots hold the soil. When the trees are cut down, rain washes the soil away.
cards.12.once.secenekler.1.neden: Plant cover does not affect earthquakes.
cards.12.once.secenekler.2.neden: Other gases cause the thinning of the ozone layer.
cards.13.p:
• Plants are eukaryotic, multicellular, have cellulose walls and protect an embryo.
• Mosses are nonvascular and seedless. Ferns are vascular, but seedless.
• The gametophyte is dominant in mosses, and the sporophyte in all other plants.
• In gymnosperms the seed is exposed, and in angiosperms it is inside a fruit.
• Monocots have parallel veins and fibrous roots.
quiz.0.q: Put the life cycle of a fern in order, starting with the sporophyte.
quiz.0.ogeler.0: The sporophyte (2n) makes spores (n) by meiosis
quiz.0.ogeler.1: The spore grows by mitosis and forms the gametophyte (prothallus)
quiz.0.ogeler.2: The gametophyte makes gametes by mitosis
quiz.0.ogeler.3: The gametes fuse and form a zygote (2n)
quiz.0.ogeler.4: The zygote grows and forms a new sporophyte
quiz.0.e: The sporophyte makes haploid spores by meiosis, and a spore grows by mitosis into the gametophyte. The gametophyte makes gametes by mitosis. The diploid zygote formed by fertilization grows into a sporophyte again.
quiz.1.q: Sort each feature into monocot or dicot.
quiz.1.e: In monocots, veins are parallel, bundles are scattered, roots are fibrous and flower parts come in multiples of 3. In dicots, veins form a network, bundles are arranged in a ring and there is a taproot. Their embryos have two cotyledons.
quiz.2.q: The cells of a moss's green, leafy plant have 10 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in the cells of this moss's sporophyte?
quiz.2.e: The green plant we see in a moss is the gametophyte, and n = 10. The sporophyte grows from the zygote formed when two gametes fuse. That is why it has 2n = 20 chromosomes.
quiz.3.q: What is the main feature that sets a pine apart from an apple tree?
quiz.3.o.0: The apple's seed is inside a fruit, and the pine's is exposed.
quiz.3.o.1: The pine reproduces by spores, and the apple by seeds.
quiz.3.o.2: The apple has vascular bundles, and the pine does not.
quiz.3.o.3: The pine does not photosynthesize, and the apple does.
quiz.3.e: Both are vascular seed plants. The difference lies in how the seed is protected. A pine is a gymnosperm and has no flowers or fruit. An apple tree is an angiosperm.
quiz.3.y.1: A pine also reproduces by seeds. The difference is whether the seed is inside a fruit or exposed.
quiz.3.y.2: A pine is also a vascular plant. The main difference is whether the seed is enclosed in a fruit.
quiz.3.y.3: A pine has green leaves and carries out photosynthesis. The difference is whether the seed is exposed or enclosed.
A:baslik: The plant kingdom and plant groups
A:ozet: Try first, then learn the name. Use switches to find a group, move water up and play through alternation of generations.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Flip the switches and find which group the pine belongs to.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: A pine is a gymnosperm. It has vascular bundles and seeds, but no flowers or fruit.
A:adimlar.1.metin: Two stems get water from below at the same time. One has no vascular bundles (xylem), and the other has them.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.soru: In which one does the water reach the top?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Water moving from cell to cell is very slow. A pipe-like path carries water much faster.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Xylem carries water up quickly, like a pipe. In the stem without bundles, water passes slowly from cell to cell.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: In the stem without bundles, water only moves slowly from cell to cell.
A:adimlar.2.metin: The leaf cells of a fern have 24 chromosomes (2n = 24). The leaf makes spores by meiosis, and meiosis halves the chromosome number. A spore grows by mitosis, which keeps the number the same, and becomes a small heart-shaped plant called the prothallus.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: How many chromosomes are in the cells of the heart-shaped prothallus?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The prothallus is not the sporophyte. It is the gametophyte, and it grows from a spore made by meiosis.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: The spore forms by meiosis and is n = 12. The prothallus grows from the spore by mitosis, and mitosis does not change the chromosome number.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: In alternation of generations, the chromosome number goes from n to 2n only at fertilization. No 4n cells form.
A:adimlar.3.metin: One of the two generations is large and long-lived. It is called the dominant generation. Change the group and compare the size of the gametophyte and the sporophyte.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.soru: How do the generations change from mosses to seed plants?
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Set the group to 3. In a seed plant, the gametophyte is only as big as a pollen grain or an embryo sac.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: The green mat we see in a moss is the gametophyte, while the large plant we see in a fern is the sporophyte. In seed plants, the gametophyte stays microscopic.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Look at the bars. In every group, one generation is much larger than the other.
A:adimlar.4.metin: Watch what happens after fertilization in a pine and an apple.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.soru: In which one does the seed stay inside a fruit?
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: An apple is an angiosperm. The ovule is protected in the flower's ovary, and the seed stays inside the fruit.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: In a pine, the seed sits exposed on the scale of the female cone. There is no ovary, so no flower or fruit forms.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: A fruit develops from an ovary. A pine has no flower or ovary, so it forms no fruit.
A:adimlar.5.metin: The rose on the screen is a dicot. Change its features and turn it into a tulip with 6 tepals.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.tamam: A tulip is a monocot. Its 6 tepals (a multiple of 3), parallel veins and fibrous root show this together.
A:kapanis.0: Plants are eukaryotic, multicellular, have cellulose walls and protect an embryo. Most make their own food by photosynthesis.
A:kapanis.1: Mosses are nonvascular and seedless, while ferns are vascular but seedless. Gymnosperms and angiosperms are both vascular and have seeds.
A:kapanis.2: In alternation of generations, the 2n sporophyte makes spores by meiosis. Gametes form by mitosis in the n gametophyte.
A:kapanis.3: The gametophyte is dominant in mosses, and the sporophyte is dominant in ferns and seed plants.
A:kapanis.4: In gymnosperms the seed is exposed on a scale, and in angiosperms it is inside a fruit. Monocots have flower parts in multiples of 3, parallel veins and fibrous roots.
